episode.title: Restore extension module loading inside the compiled runtime
episode.before: At parent 53d9e61bac3408b4ff6b4ccf9dd49e1c4c9640b1, the extension loader exposed the host package to compiled-runtime extensions through a lazy require of the public index. The public index simultaneously re-exported loader functions, creating a loader-to-index-to-loader cycle. The compiled-runtime virtual module table omitted the agent-core package, the development alias table omitted the same package, and the root compilation dependency graph resolved @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.2. The changelog states that extensions with local file imports did not work correctly in the compiled Bun binary.
episode.after: At 843f2352518cb75343f9e6e47bb86f708e1f4769, loader functions are no longer re-exported from the public index, allowing the loader to statically import the initialized public API without a circular dependency. The virtual module table now directly supplies bundled namespaces for the coding-agent API and agent-core API, while the development alias table resolves agent-core from the filesystem. The root package and lockfile select @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.5, described by the commit and changelog as bundling the transformation support required by the compiled runtime. Extension discovery and SDK/CLI call sites continue importing loader operations through the internal extensions module.
episode.diff: The implementation removes createExtensionRuntime, discoverAndLoadExtensions, and loadExtensions from the package-root value exports; replaces the lazy public-API getter and runtime require with a static index import and direct virtual-module entry; adds agent-core to both compiled-runtime virtual modules and development aliases; and upgrades the root jiti dependency and lockfile resolution from 2.6.2 to 2.6.5. Documentation terminology was also updated, but no regression test or compiled-binary validation artifact was added in the pinned commit.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 843f2352518cb75343f9e6e47bb86f708e1f4769 identifies the resolution as fixing extension loading in a Bun binary and explicitly lists cycle removal, static public-index import, agent-core virtual-module support, and the jiti 2.6.5 update.

The parent loader lazily required ../../index.js from the @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent virtual-module getter because loader.ts was part of the public index, while the parent public index re-exported createExtensionRuntime, discoverAndLoadExtensions, and loadExtensions.

The change removes loader operations from the package-root value exports and replaces the lazy require-backed virtual-module getter with a static ../../index.js namespace import and direct table entry.
The updated loader statically imports the coding-agent, agent-core, AI, TUI, and TypeBox namespaces and supplies them through VIRTUAL_MODULES when isBunBinary is true with tryNative disabled.
The updated non-binary alias map adds @mariozechner/pi-agent-core through require.resolve while retaining aliases for the coding-agent API, AI, TUI, and TypeBox.

The loader selects virtual modules with tryNative disabled only for a compiled Bun binary and selects filesystem aliases for Node/development execution; isBunBinary is derived from Bun virtual-filesystem markers in import.meta.url.
The root package adds @mariozechner/jiti ^2.6.5 and the lockfile changes its resolved version from 2.6.2 to 2.6.5; the commit says this version bundles Babel for Bun-binary compatibility.
evidence_units.source: git diff 53d9e61bac3408b4ff6b4ccf9dd49e1c4c9640b1 843f2352518cb75343f9e6e47bb86f708e1f4769 -- package.json package-lock.json; git show --format=%B --no-patch 843f2352518cb75343f9e6e47bb86f708e1f4769

evidence_units.claim: The CLI continues to call loadExtensions for explicit paths and discoverAndLoadExtensions for configured and discovered paths through the internal core/extensions index, so narrowing package-root exports does not remove the internal loading path.

The SDK imports loader operations from ./extensions/index.js and uses discoverAndLoadExtensions for discovery and createExtensionRuntime for inline extensions, independently of the package-root re-exports removed by the change.

The pinned tree's extension-discovery tests exercise TypeScript extension loading, host TypeBox imports, third-party imports, local dependency resolution, explicit loading, discovery, and error reporting, but contain no compiled-Bun-binary regression case for local file imports or agent-core imports.
The changelog records the intended externally observable result: compiled Bun binary extensions with local file imports work correctly after the change.

The pinned commit changes seven implementation, dependency, changelog, and documentation files and changes no test file, so repository evidence does not establish an automated compiled-binary regression oracle for this fix.

candidate_atomics.name: decouple-loader-from-public-entrypoint
candidate_atomics.title: Break the loader/public-entrypoint import cycle
candidate_atomics.description: Keep loader-only operations behind an internal module boundary so the loader can statically reference the host package's initialized public API for extension imports.

semantic_action.intent: Make the host package API available to dynamically loaded extensions without recursively initializing the extension loader through the public entrypoint.
semantic_action.module_role: extension loader and public API boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The loader obtains the public API through a lazy runtime require, while the public API re-exports loader operations and therefore points back to the loader during initialization.
semantic_action.post_state: Loader operations remain reachable through internal extension modules, but the public entrypoint no longer value-re-exports them, so the loader can statically import a stable public API namespace.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the module graph to confirm that the loader imports the public entrypoint, the public entrypoint does not value-export loader operations, and existing CLI/SDK loading call sites resolve those operations through the internal extension module.
parameters: internal CLI and SDK call sites

candidate_atomics.name: supply-host-modules-across-runtime-resolution-modes
candidate_atomics.title: Provide extension imports through runtime-specific module maps
candidate_atomics.description: Statically retain host modules for compiled execution and mirror their identities with filesystem aliases during development execution.

semantic_action.intent: Allow extension source to import supported host APIs when ordinary filesystem package resolution is unavailable inside a compiled executable, while preserving development-mode resolution.
semantic_action.pre_state: The compiled-runtime virtual module table lacks at least one supported host package and obtains the main host API through a lazy require; the development alias table also lacks that host package.
semantic_action.post_state: Every supported host package needed by extensions has a statically bundled namespace in compiled mode and a corresponding resolvable alias in development mode; compiled mode routes all imports through the transformer with native resolution disabled.
semantic_action.validation: Load an extension that imports the public host API, agent-core API, TypeBox, and a local file in both development mode and the compiled executable; require zero loader errors and successful extension registration. Existing tests cover several development-mode imports but not the compiled-executable branch.

candidate_atomics.name: bundle-extension-transformer-dependency
candidate_atomics.title: Include the compatible source transformer in the executable dependency graph
candidate_atomics.description: Select the transformer release that packages the parsing/transformation support needed when extension source and its local imports are evaluated inside the compiled runtime.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure the compiled executable contains the transformation machinery required to evaluate extension source and transitive local imports.
semantic_action.pre_state: The root compilation graph resolves transformer version 2.6.2, and compiled extensions with local file imports are reported as not working correctly.
semantic_action.post_state: The root compilation graph resolves transformer version 2.6.5, which the resolution records as bundling the required Babel support for the compiled runtime.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the root manifest and lockfile for the selected version, then build the executable and load an extension with a local TypeScript import; successful registration without a transformation or resolution error is the runtime oracle.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-compiled-extension-module-loading
candidate_workflows.title: Restore extension imports in a compiled executable
candidate_workflows.description: Repair extension loading when a compiled runtime cannot resolve or transform the same host-package and local-file imports that work during development.

workflow_graph.goal: Make extensions with host-package imports and transitive local source imports load successfully in both development execution and the compiled executable.
when_to_use: Extensions load in a normal filesystem-backed runtime but fail after the host application is compiled into a single executable.
The extension loader relies on dynamic evaluation and extensions import host packages or local TypeScript modules that are not independently present in the executable filesystem.
Making the host public API statically available to the loader currently creates an entrypoint/loader initialization cycle.
anti_goals: Do not redesign extension discovery, registration, or execution lifecycle when the failure is confined to module resolution and transformation.
Do not expose loader-internal operations from the public package entrypoint merely to preserve an accidental export surface.
Do not replace supported host package imports with copied extension-local implementations.
Do not treat documentation changes or a successful development-mode test as proof that the compiled executable path works.
not_applicable_when: The host is not compiled and ordinary package/filesystem resolution is available in every supported deployment.
The failure occurs after an extension factory has loaded and is caused by runtime event handling, reload state, or extension business logic.
The extension imports an unsupported external package that is neither intended to be bundled nor installed beside the extension.
No reproducible extension import failure or compiled-runtime execution path can be established.
inputs: A parent and fixed implementation of the extension loader
The compiled-runtime detector and executable build command
The supported host package identities exposed to extensions
An extension fixture importing host APIs and a transitive local TypeScript file
The transformer package version and resolved lockfile entry
CLI and SDK loader call sites
workflow_graph.entry_state: Development-mode extension loading exists, but compiled execution cannot reliably resolve or transform supported host imports and transitive local files; the loader/public-entrypoint graph also prevents a direct static host-API mapping.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The loader/public-entrypoint graph is acyclic, compiled execution receives statically retained supported modules, development execution receives equivalent filesystem aliases, a compatible transformer is included in the executable dependency graph, and the same extension fixture registers successfully in both runtime modes.

steps.condition: Required when the loader must statically import the public API and the public entrypoint currently value-exports loader operations.
steps.validation: Confirm there is no public-entrypoint-to-loader value-export edge while CLI and SDK call sites still reach loader operations through an internal module.

steps.condition: Required when compiled execution lacks filesystem package resolution but extension imports must retain their documented package identities.
steps.validation: Confirm compiled mode uses direct bundled namespaces with native resolution disabled and development mode maps the same supported package identities to filesystem-resolvable targets.

steps.condition: Required when the executable's current transformer package does not include the parser/transformer support needed for transitive extension source imports.
steps.validation: Confirm the manifest and lockfile resolve the compatible transformer release, then load a fixture with a transitive local TypeScript import in the built executable.

validation_ladder: Static module-graph check: the loader may import the public entrypoint, but the public entrypoint must not value-export loader operations.
Resolution-table check: every supported host import has a compiled virtual-module namespace and a development alias where filesystem resolution is used.
Dependency check: the executable's root dependency graph and lockfile select the compatible transformer release.
Development regression check: existing extension discovery, host-library import, third-party dependency, explicit loading, and error-reporting tests continue to pass.

Compiled-runtime regression check: build the executable and load an extension importing the public host API, agent-core API, TypeBox, and a transitive local TypeScript file; require no loader errors and successful registration.
stop_conditions: Stop if removing the public loader exports would remove an intentional supported API rather than an accidental cycle; explicit product direction is then required.
Stop if the failing import is not part of the supported extension module contract and should remain external.
Stop if the compiled executable cannot be built or executed, because development-mode results cannot validate the affected branch.
Stop promotion as fully validated until a compiled-runtime regression oracle is executed or added.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned commit contains no automated compiled-Bun-binary regression test and the evidence bundle contains no CI or manual test result.
The issue body, PR body, reviews, status checks, and failure trace are unavailable, so the exact pre-fix error message and minimal failing extension are unknown.
The repository evidence attributes the required transformation support to jiti 2.6.5, but the upstream release notes were not included in the supplied evidence.
The package-root loader exports were removed intentionally, but no available discussion establishes whether they had been considered a supported public API.

unresolved_questions: Was a compiled Bun executable manually built and tested with an extension containing a local file import before the commit was merged?
What exact loader or transformer error occurred in the parent state?
Should the removed package-root loader operations be treated as intentionally unsupported internals or as a breaking SDK surface change?
